bullets: Game 2 of an 8-game session (video 161.3s-329.3s) against Giant / Prince / Dark Prince / Mega Minion / Bomber / Bats / Rage. Won on the overtime damage lead: enemy right tower 4858 -> 353, his own towers 4858 / 4781 — "that is going to be good game. Very nice win" (322-323s).

The whole gameplan is Ronin-first defence into free chip. Four Ronin deploy labels (clock 2:42 [9, 7], 2:03 [14, 10], 0:52 [8, 0], 0:27 [0, 13]), each onto a melee push, and every Goblin Barrel (2:17, 1:36, 1:14) goes down in the lane the Ronin has just cleared.

The support cards are all defensive specialists that cover what the Ronin cannot: Tesla as the pin (2:03, 0:58, 0:33, 0:17), Royal Delivery for the air support (1:53, 1:16, 0:43, 0:17), Skeletons and Fire Spirit as one-elixir layers. Ryley states the design at 272-276s: "I feel like my deck right here covers a lot of the weaknesses that can come from playing with the Ronin."

Offence is cheap and opportunistic — Wall Breakers split at the bridge to open (2:48) and the Evo pair sent as a counter-attack from inside a defence (0:27, "Let's Evo wall breakers to pressure him while defending"), plus barrels on cycle. He never builds a big push.

The Magic Archer is the flexible slot: "if you don't have the hero [Magic Archer], you can always use the dart goblin in this deck as well... but you can always like replace it with the hero goblins" (192-202s).

Ryley's own caveat on the list: it is matchup-dependent. "against say a Lava Hound deck, Ronin is absolutely terrible or like maybe even a bait match up, it's really bad. But then when you're in like a match up like this, it's just like the best card you could ever have" (258-270s). His pitch for the video's 96% claim is defensive: "nothing can actually break through if you play it properly" (319-320s).

new_deck.rationale: Goblin Barrel, Wall Breakers, Skeletons and Fire Spirit all demand the same small spell while Tesla and Royal Delivery hold the ground, and at ~2.8 average elixir the deck cycles back to whichever threat is unanswered.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The Ronin is a 5 elixir mini-tank whose Parry blocks and reflects melee attacks, so against melee-heavy decks a single Ronin can eat a Dark Prince and a Mega Minion and still walk in for tower damage — in this match that one defence took the enemy right tower from 4858 to 2891. Everything else in the list covers a Ronin weakness: Tesla and Royal Delivery answer the air and the building-targeters he cannot touch, Skeletons and Fire Spirit are one-elixir layers that stop him from being swarmed, and the Magic Archer gives the deck range. Offence is deliberately cheap — Goblin Barrel and Wall Breakers chip on cycle behind whatever the Ronin has just killed, which is why the enemy tower falls in steps rather than to one big push. Ryley is explicit that the shell exists to patch the win condition ("I feel like my deck right here covers a lot of the weaknesses that can come from playing with the Ronin") and equally explicit about its ceiling: the Ronin is near-useless against air decks like Lava Hound and against bait, so the 96% claim is a matchup-dependent one.
